Prepared 19 September 2026

Scope: swaps, yield strategies, staking, lending, borrowing, liquidity provision, portfolio, risk, activity, partner SDK and production operations.

Executive decision

Project boundary: this document covers only the CapitalOS platform and its Everything Stacks consumer application. Its backlog, architecture and frontend direction are derived from the CapitalOS repository and specifications; no external project is used as its implementation baseline.
Build orchestration, evidence and user experience—not replacement DeFi infrastructure. CapitalOS integrates verified deployments of sBTC, Zest, Bitflow, Hermetica, Granite and supported stacking providers. User wallets sign direct protocol transactions. Everything Stacks consumes the same public SDK shipped to partners.

In scope

  • Protocol adapters and capability registry
  • Evidence-gated reads, quotes and unsigned plans
  • Durable workflow/recovery and canonical reconciliation
  • Everything Stacks production frontend
  • Partner SDK, hooks, components and example
  • Security, accessibility, observability and release operations

Explicitly out of scope

  • Pooled custodial strategy vaults
  • Private-key custody or unrestricted signing
  • Invented rates, prices, liquidity or history
  • Guaranteed APY or liquidation prevention
  • Permissionless arbitrary contract routing
  • Automatic retry of uncertain writes

Architecture and responsibility boundaries

Protocol source of truth

Deployed contracts and canonical chain evidence define balances, positions and action outcomes.

CapitalOS

Normalizes evidence, builds guarded unsigned plans, persists workflows and reconciles results.

Everything Stacks

Explains, simulates, reviews and invokes public SDK commands; it never constructs protocol calls.

Non-negotiable financial-data rules

  • Unknown, unsupported, stale and disputed are explicit states—not zero.
  • Every amount has a canonical asset ID and integer/base-unit representation.
  • Every price/rate/liquidity datum carries source, timestamp/block and confidence/evidence state.
  • Provider-reported returns remain labeled and cannot become verified through repetition.
  • Recommendations require both usable return evidence and deployable-capacity evidence.
  • Historical charts contain canonical observations only; earned yield requires reconciled cash flows.
  • Quotes are informational; plans bind expiry, network, registry, adapter and deployment versions.
  • A workflow is complete only after canonical position reconciliation.

Shared action lifecycle

Choose → Quote → Review → Wallet sign → Submit → Confirm → Reconcile → Receipt / recovery

Definition of Ready

  • Dependencies and protocol access are available.
  • Exact deployment, asset identifiers and evidence requirements are named.
  • Acceptance evidence and reviewer are defined.
  • Unknown product/financial semantics are resolved before implementation.

Definition of Done

  • Acceptance checklist is complete and reviewer reproduced the result.
  • PR references task and requirement IDs.
  • Unit/integration/E2E or live-transaction evidence is linked as appropriate.
  • Data source, network, registry, adapter and calculation versions are recorded.
  • Failure, stale, partial, rejection and reload behavior are covered.
  • Documentation, telemetry and rollback/recovery instructions are updated.
No schedule promise is implied. Estimates are focused engineering days. One implementation task and one review maximum per engineer; tasks exceeding two days must be split.

Frontend visual direction and screen contract

Rendered Everything Stacks wireframes: the following nine images—including the public landing page—define the intended information hierarchy, density, visual language and financial disclosures. They are deliberately distinct from other products. Values are illustrative UI copy, not live protocol evidence. Final implementation may refine styling, but it must preserve the states, evidence labels and shared transaction lifecycle shown here.

Frontend state matrix

StateUser-facing requirementAction policy
LoadingSingle-line purpose-specific message, stable layout and cancellable/retryable reads.No signing; preserve prior verified data if clearly timestamped.
EmptyCentered instruction with address input or wallet connection.Offer the next valid read-only or setup action.
PartialShow verified subtotal and explicitly name excluded positions.Unrelated verified reads remain available; unsafe writes fail closed.
UnsupportedName the asset/protocol capability and why it is unsupported.No invented value or executable control.
Stale/disputedShow age, sources and disagreement.Require refresh/requote; cannot rank or recommend.
ReviewGive/receive, fees, minimum output, debt change, health, protocol and contract.Wallet invocation only after SDK plan validation.
SubmittedTxid, explorer, confirmation/reconciliation distinction and next action.Never auto-retry uncertain writes.
Failed/delayedPlain-language cause, funds status and recovery path.Resume, requote, switch network, provide fee, reclaim or contact support.

Responsive and accessibility contract

  • Keyboard-complete action flows and visible focus.
  • Focus returns correctly after wallet/error modals.
  • Workflow progress uses live regions; risk is never communicated by color alone.
  • Every amount includes its asset unit; addresses truncate safely and remain copyable.
  • Tables become labeled cards below tablet width.
  • No overlapping chart labels, clipped identifiers or ambiguous negative-number formatting.

Production release gates

Code and SDK

  • Typecheck, unit, integration, E2E and production build green
  • Published-package clean-install test
  • OpenAPI/runtime schema agreement
  • No forbidden application-to-adapter imports

Financial integrity

  • Projection/backfill audit complete
  • Golden-address and independent reconciliation pass
  • Stale/partial/unsupported gates proven
  • Exact arithmetic and post-conditions audited

Security and recovery

  • No unresolved critical/high finding
  • Wallet rejection, expiry, reorg and broadcast uncertainty tested
  • Registry pause and safe-exit-only behavior proven
  • Backup restore and provider-outage drills complete

Product and operations

  • All entry and exit journeys pass
  • Accessibility and wallet/browser matrix pass
  • Dashboards, alerts, incident/support ownership active
  • Five pilot users and one partner certification complete

Required launch evidence bundle

ArtifactMust contain
Release manifestGit SHA, package versions, registry version, adapter versions, migrations and feature flags.
Protocol certificationDeployment, block/snapshot, fixtures, live workflow/transaction IDs and known limitations.
Product acceptanceDesktop/mobile captures, E2E runs, accessibility report and recovery demonstrations.
Data integrityGolden-address comparison, pricing quorum, projection audit, backfill completeness and reconciliation.
Security and operationsThreat model, findings, restore/outage drill, monitors, alert routes and incident owners.
Go/no-go recordPilot results, partner certification, exclusions, rollback triggers and accountable approvers.
Launch stop conditions: stale evidence can influence a recommendation; an unapproved contract can be called; a signed action can be duplicated; portfolio/debt cannot reconcile; an entry path lacks a tested exit; or any critical/high security finding remains open.
